report.tagline: India's largest eyewear brand, selling its own glasses and lenses through 3,600+ stores and an app, made in its own factory.
report.simpleSummary: Lenskart sells glasses, sunglasses and contact lenses under its own brands like Vincent Chase and John Jacobs. You can get a free eye test in a store or at home, try frames on virtually in the app, and get glasses delivered in a few days. Because it makes its own frames and lenses, prices start low, around ₹1,000 to ₹2,000. A yearly Gold membership gives buy-one-get-one deals, which keeps customers coming back.

overview.whatItDoes: Lenskart designs, makes and sells eyewear. It runs stores across India and abroad, an app and website, and home eye tests. It controls the full chain from factory to store, so it can sell good glasses cheaply and still make money.
howItWorks: Customers get a free eye test in a store, at home, or upload their prescription.
They choose frames in store or try them on in the app with 3D virtual try-on.
Lenses are cut and fitted at Lenskart's large factory in Hyderabad, designed for 5 crore pairs a year.
Glasses are delivered home or picked up in store, usually within days.
Gold members (yearly fee) get buy-one-get-one and other deals.
Abroad, it owns Owndays (Japan) and stores in Singapore, UAE and others.
overview.valueProposition: For customers: stylish glasses at fair prices, with free eye tests and easy try-on. For Lenskart: owning the product, the factory and the store means high margins and a direct link to customers.

businessModel.summary: Lenskart makes most money selling its own glasses and lenses at high gross margins, plus Gold membership fees. It is profitable with strong store economics.

businessModel.pricing: Frames start around ₹500 to ₹1,000; most glasses with lenses cost ₹1,500 to ₹5,000; India average selling price about ₹1,950. Eye tests are free. Gold membership is a yearly fee (around ₹500 to ₹600, often discounted).
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a ₹2,000 pair of glasses, Lenskart's cost to make the frame and lens might be ₹500 to ₹600 because it makes them itself. After store, staff, delivery and marketing costs, it keeps roughly ₹200 to ₹300 as profit. In India, EBITDA before lease costs was 16% of revenue in Q2 FY27. Each new store pays back in a few years if it sells steady volumes.

howTheyGetUsers: Opening about 140 new India stores a quarter
growth.moat: Lenskart's moat is control of the whole chain: design, factory, stores and app. Rivals would need years and big money to build both a factory and over 2,800 stores in India.

pmLessons: Owning the supply chain lets you cut prices and still make profit.
Online and offline together beat either alone for products people want to try.
Paid memberships like Gold drive repeat buying.
A free service (eye tests) can be the main way to win customers.
